Lina: Heads up — saw a customer report where our demo chat shows two completions after flaky mobile networks. First completion is truncated, then a second full completion arrives a second later.
Jin: Interesting. Which client path are they using?
Lina: They said mobile web demo, WKWebView on iOS 15. Sequence: send long prompt, then lock screen/unlock quickly.
QA-Rita: Repro steps I captured: open demo, send message, home button (background) for ~700ms, foreground again. Repro ~60%. Attached network log shows connection closed and reopened.
Marco: That hints at resume + replay. Do we include sequence numbers in the SSE comments?
Jin: Server emits `: resume_id=kk2 seq=541` comments, but our browser fetch wrapper ignores comments and just concatenates decoded chunks.
Lina: Our parser splits on "\n\n" and JSON.parse each data block. When reconnect happens we simply append new bytes to the tail and try again. That means a partial JSON from before disconnect can get merged with replayed bytes and produce duplicates.
QA-Rita: Console sometimes shows `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` before we recover, and UI ends up rendering two final tokens.
Marco: Two areas to address: (1) text decoding edgecases — split UTF-8 codepoints across chunks; (2) ordering/duplication caused by replayed seqs.
Jin: Plan: use TextDecoder with streaming decode and keep a byteTail between reads so we never decode half a codepoint. Also parse SSE comment lines ASAP to extract resume_id and seq.
Lina: After we parse seq, we should surface it on the sample app (small badge) so customers see if their client is falling behind.
Marco: For duplication, client should maintain a bounded recentSeq window and dedupe tokens by seq+offset. If reconnect shows seq <= lastAppliedSeq, ignore duplicates. If seq jumps backward significantly, emit `seq_regress` telemetry and fallback to a full fetch non-streaming path.
Jin: Add a feature flag `strict_sse_seq` default false. If enabled, the client will fail fast on any out-of-order seq and surface an error to the app. Otherwise we attempt to reconcile with dedupe.
QA-Rita: I'll add e2e harness that toggles network via Chrome Remote Debugging with timings matching iOS background/foreground behavior. Will include a capture of raw bytes, decoded text, and parsed seqs for any failing runs.
Marco: Also add a unit that injects overlapping replay where server replays from an earlier seq to ensure the dedupe set works. Keep window size at 1024 entries to avoid memory growth.
Jin: Small UX fix while we ship: defensive ignore repeated `[DONE]` tokens for the same seq to avoid flash duplicates. That will be low-risk.
Lina: Can we also add a short note in the sample README about seq semantics and how to enable strict mode? Many customers run the demo and copy the code, we should guide them.
sdk-bot: Created tracking ticket RED-1254: "browser-sse: decode tail + seq parse + dedupe window" and assigned to @Jin.
ops-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: browser-sdk@0.22.0-canary.1 to staging at 01:00 UTC.
Jin: I'll open a minimal PR with the decoder tail + seq parse + dedupe logic behind a flag. If QA validates the canary, we'll flip the flag on staging and run the mobile harness.
QA-Rita: Once canary is up I'll run tests across iOS 13-16 and Android webview. If it still repros, I'll attach console logs and the sequence timeline.
Lina: Thanks team — sounds low-risk and should improve demo stability and give customers better observability into stream ordering. :raised_hands:
